description: Hi! I’m a passionate developer and space tech enthusiast looking to build an innovative project for the NASA Space Apps Challenge. I specialize in full-stack web development, Python, and data visualization. I love tackling complex problems, analyzing satellite data, and building clean UI/UX interfaces.
summary:
BengalFlare is an open-source Earth observation platform that resolves the 2012 satellite sensor discontinuity to establish a unified, multi-decadal global fire history. For 24+ years, NASA monitored thermal anomalies via MODIS (1 km nadir) and VIIRS (375 m), but the sensor shift caused an artificial ~380% surge in recorded hotspots. BengalFlare directly addresses the NASA Space Apps "Harmonization of MODIS and VIIRS Hot Spots" challenge by deploying physics-informed machine learning to harmonize cross-sensor resolution disparities across five polar satellites (Terra, Aqua, Suomi-NPP, NOAA-20, NOAA-21), while accounting for monsoon cloud-cover blindspots with a daily Observability Index.

This harmonization is critical: fragmented records distort climate baselines and undermine disaster preparedness. By anchoring active NASA FIRMS detections against a calibrated 24-year baseline, BengalFlare fuses live atmospheric forecasts to predict forward wildfire spread corridors, classify fire origin (differentiating agricultural stubble burns from forest wildfires), and autonomously dispatch real-time early warnings via Telegram and webhooks—empowering first responders and protecting vulnerable communities before flames arrive.
details:
### 1. What It Does & How It Works

BengalFlare is an open-source, sensor-agnostic Earth observation and wildfire early warning platform. It reconciles 24+ years (2000–present) of active-fire observations across five NASA and NOAA polar-orbiting satellites: Terra and Aqua (MODIS) alongside Suomi-NPP, NOAA-20, and NOAA-21 (VIIRS).

The platform operates through two interconnected engines:

* **Sensor Harmonization Engine:** In 2012, transitioning from MODIS (1,000 m nadir) to VIIRS (375 m) caused an artificial +380% surge in reported fire detections. BengalFlare bridges this resolution discontinuity using cross-sensor coincident overpass calibration. It benchmarks six mathematical models (B0–B5), deploying Two-Stage Quantile Random Forests (QRF) to generate unified historical burning baselines with uncertainty bounds. Crucially, it accounts for tropical monsoon cloud-masking blindspots through a daily Observability Index (OI), distinguishing "unobserved due to clouds" from "no active burning."

* **Real-Time Early Warning & Threat Engine:** Anchored against the calibrated 24-year baseline, BengalFlare continuously polls NASA FIRMS real-time thermal telemetry and Open-Meteo meteorological forecasts. It calculates Fosberg Fire Danger Indices (FDI), models Rothermel forward spread rates, and projects dynamic Huygens elliptical threat cones to determine downwind settlement impact hours before flames arrive.

---

### 2. Benefits & Intended Impact

* **Unified Climate Baseline:** Restores longitudinal consistency across 24+ years of Earth observation, enabling climatologists to study real ecological burning trends without sensor-change bias.

* **Proactive Life Safety:** Shifts disaster management from reactive firefighting to predictive early evacuation by delivering hours of actionable lead time to frontline communities.

* **Elimination of Alert Fatigue:** Integrates smart origin attribution to classify whether a thermal detection is human-made agricultural stubble burning (Aman crop residue clearance) or a dangerous forest wildfire, preventing community panic.

* **Operational Satellite Continuity:** Anticipates the late-2026 decommissioning of Suomi-NPP by providing an automated calibration handover to NOAA-20 and NOAA-21.

---

### 3. Tools, Coding Languages, Hardware & Software

* **Languages & Core Frameworks:** Python 3.10+, TypeScript, React 19, FastAPI, Vite.

* **Data Engineering & Analytical Database:** DuckDB (in-process analytical SQL engine for zero-copy Parquet queries), Apache Arrow, GeoPandas, NumPy, SciPy, scikit-learn.

* **Geospatial & Visualization:** MapLibre GL (WebGL GPU-accelerated rendering), Uber H3 hexagonal spatial indexing, NASA EOSDIS GIBS satellite basemaps.

* **Real-Time Telemetry & Dispatch:** NASA FIRMS NRT Area API, Open-Meteo Meteorological API, Telegram Bot API, Common Alerting Protocol (CAP) JSON webhooks.

* **Testing & Infrastructure:** Playwright end-to-end test suite (desktop and mobile), Pytest backend analytical suite (32 unit tests), Vercel edge deployment, GitHub Actions CI/CD watchdog.

---

### 4. Creative Innovation

* **Bridging Historical Science with Real-Time Action:** While most tools remain retrospective research papers or simple fire pinboards, BengalFlare closes the gap between 24-year satellite harmonization and real-time community alert dispatch.

* **Human-Centered Aerospace Design:** Features our custom "Cosmic Dusk & Solar Flare" glassmorphism HUD interface, converting complex radiative equations into intuitive 3D orbital globes, 24-year burning heatmaps, and clear evacuation decision cards.

* **Autonomous Spam-Free Broadcasts:** Implemented an intelligent regional dispatch engine that aggregates dozens of scattered satellite detections into a single, cohesive Regional Intelligence Bulletin on Telegram, preventing notification flooding.

---

### 5. Critical Factors Considered

* **Orbital Geometry & Sensor Physics:** Accounted for MODIS bowtie distortions, scan angle variations, pixel growth at swath edges, and saturation brightness temperatures.

* **Seasonal & Land-Use Realities:** Tailored for the Bengal Basin and global wildland-urban interfaces, factoring in post-monsoon agricultural crop clearing calendars vs. true canopy fuel moisture thresholds.

* **Accessibility & Resilience:** Engineered for zero-crash reliability with verified offline fixtures, mobile responsive layouts, WCAG AA high-contrast compliance, and direct smartphone Telegram alerts for remote forest beat officers without specialized GIS hardware.
